metadata.title: Capgo | AI-Assisted Cordova to Capacitor Migration (2026)
metadata.description: Migrate Cordova to Capacitor with an AI coding agent: Capgo's cordova-to-capacitor skill, copy-paste prompts, a Capgo plugin map, and the Capgo MCP server.

blocks.text: Give your AI coding agent a plan it can follow: install Capgo's cordova-to-capacitor skill, paste your plugin list into the prompts below, check the plugin map, and connect the Capgo MCP server to upload bundles and request builds. You review every change.
How to run the migration with an AI agent
One skill, one inventory, small reviewed steps, and a real device test before release.
Add the cordova-to-capacitor skill to your coding agent. It gives the agent the migration order and the Capacitor plugin choices.
Start with a plugin map, not code
Ask the agent to read your Cordova project and return a plugin replacement table first. Review it before any file changes.
Use the cordova-to-capacitor skill from Cap-go/capgo-skills to migrate this Cordova app to Capacitor. Start with a plugin replacement table and wait for my review before changing files.
Review each step and test on devices
Let the agent add Capacitor, move config.xml settings, and swap plugins in small commits. Test permissions, deep links, and the upgrade from your current store version on real devices.

bunx cap sync
bunx cap run ios
bunx cap run android
Connect the Capgo MCP server to ship
With the MCP server running, the agent can upload bundles, manage channels, and request native builds. Plugin changes still need a store release.
What Changes When You Leave Cordova

Capacitor is a native app that hosts your web app. You commit real Xcode and Android Studio projects, keep your existing web code, and replace Cordova plugins with Capacitor plugins. That makes the work easy to split into small steps an agent can do and you can review.
Export what you have today and keep it as your migration input:

# In your Cordova project
cordova plugin list
cordova platform ls
Plugin variables (API keys, manifest placeholders, URL schemes)
2) Add Capacitor to Your Web App

bun add @capacitor/ios @capacitor/android
bunx cap add ios
bunx cap add android

bun run build
bunx cap sync
Replace high-risk plugins first: login, payments, storage, and background services. Capgo plugins are free and open source under MPL-2.0, and on any Capgo plan your plugin bug reports get priority.
Browse Capgo's plugin catalog and map by capability:
These prompts are designed to produce usable outputs (tables, checklists, plans), not vague advice.
Prompt 1: Build a Plugin Replacement Plan

You are a senior Capacitor engineer.

I am migrating a Cordova app to Capacitor. Here is my `cordova plugin list` output:
<PASTE HERE>

1) Create a table mapping each Cordova plugin to a recommended Capacitor alternative.
2) Prefer official Capacitor plugins when possible.
3) When official plugins are limited (background geolocation, social login, biometrics, IAP, in-app browser, live updates), recommend Capgo plugins:
- @capgo/background-geolocation
- @capgo/capacitor-social-login
- @capgo/capacitor-native-biometric
- @capgo/native-purchases
- @capgo/capacitor-inappbrowser
- @capgo/capacitor-updater
4) For each mapping, list migration steps and common pitfalls.
Return a prioritized plan (highest risk first).
Prompt 2: Convert config.xml Preferences Into Capacitor + Native Changes

You are migrating Cordova to Capacitor.

Here is my Cordova `config.xml`:
<PASTE HERE>

Create a migration checklist:
1) What goes into capacitor.config.ts (appId, appName, webDir, server config for dev only).
2) What must be moved to iOS (Info.plist, entitlements, URL schemes, permissions strings).
3) What must be moved to Android (AndroidManifest, Gradle, intent filters, permissions).
Be explicit about file names and what to change.

You are the QA lead for a Cordova -> Capacitor migration.

App description:
<PASTE HERE>

Features that rely on native plugins:
<LIST HERE>

Create a test plan for iOS and Android that includes:
- permission flows (fresh install, denied, restricted, limited)
- background behavior (if any)
- deep links / universal links (if any)
- upgrade path from the existing Cordova app version
Output as a checklist that an engineer can run in 2-3 hours per release candidate.

Skills give your agent a tested playbook instead of guesses. The cordova-to-capacitor skill covers the migration order. capacitor-plugins helps pick and install plugins, and capgo-live-updates sets up the updater after the move. The skills are open source and install with one command.

After you log in with the Capgo CLI, run the local MCP server so your agent can list apps, upload bundles, manage channels, check native compatibility, and request native builds. A remote MCP server at capgo.app/mcp covers docs discovery and does not change your account.

Can an AI agent migrate a Cordova app on its own?

It can do most of the mechanical work: adding Capacitor, moving config.xml settings, and swapping plugins. You still review the changes, test on real devices, and handle signing and the store release.
Which Capgo skill should we install?
Start with cordova-to-capacitor. Add capacitor-plugins for plugin choices and capgo-live-updates when you set up live updates after the move. One command installs the whole set if you prefer.
What can the Capgo MCP server do?
The local server can list and create apps, upload and list bundles, manage channels, check native compatibility, read stats, and request native builds. It uses your Capgo CLI login.
Do the Capgo plugins in the map cost anything?
No. Capgo plugins are open source under MPL-2.0. A Capgo plan adds live updates, native builds, and priority handling of your plugin bug reports.
What if the agent gets stuck?
Hand the hard parts to our team. We run Cordova to Capacitor migrations as fixed-price projects, and Premium Support gives you direct access to Capacitor engineers.
